scope: TODO graph.editor.connection-routing step 6: encoding/drawable-wait attribution of the existing visible native Metal traces. Analysis-only change; no new timing capture, application or routing behavior change.
methodology: Reanalyze the previously accepted single five-second Metal capture per scale using the unchanged trace-relative [1s,4s] window and exact owned PID. Join command-buffer-level Encoding intervals to the source artifact's accepted GPU buffers by numeric command-buffer identity and verify the label. Ignore nested encoder intervals. Require the entire Encoding interval as well as the source GPU interval to fit the analysis window. Retain process-owned Wait for Next Drawable rows intersecting the window, including boundary-crossing waits, and union their per-buffer intersections only on the same numeric thread identity. Percentiles are nearest-rank single-capture observations, not repeated-run estimates or speedups.
fixture: Same native paired-builtins-fanout-v1 documents, 100 nodes/500 connections and 500 nodes/2000 connections, default split panels and 100% graph zoom, most nodes offscreen. Isolated unavailable execution, empty viewer, --always-on-top and checked post-measurement screenshots. Host, CPU completion reports and original GPU observations remain in the source artifact.
retention: The encoding field of the analyzer output is retained below; unchanged GPU output remains in the source artifact. All selected encoding intervals and intersecting process-owned drawable waits are normalized without process names or unrelated process data. Source XML hashes match the prior artifact.
limitations: Encoding is an instrumented wall-clock interval, not measured CPU execution. PendingWrites can remain open across drawable waits. The non_drawable_wait_wall remainder is computed per buffer before taking percentiles, but still includes unrelated CPU work, scheduling, and other waits; it is not upload/staging cost. Command-buffer intervals can overlap, so totals across buffers are not frame time. Wait for Next Drawable is not frame-to-presentation latency. No CPU/GPU percentile addition/subtraction, renderer optimization, speedup, active-runtime/browser/low-zoom/drag acceptance, or 60 Hz guarantee is inferred.
